clue.text: Flower from Colorado, white one in field

parts.note: CO is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Colorado
W is the standard abbreviation for white, as on chess scoresheets
a slip is a fielder standing beside the wicketkeeper in cricket

explanation.surface: A wild flower from Colorado, a white one spotted growing in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the slips are close fielders beside the wicketkeeper, so 'one in field' is a slip, not a plant in a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a yellow-flowered wild primula of European meadows, so it is a kind of bloom.

clue.text: Charlie shoots wildly at a pair of anchors

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: wildly means the letters of shoots are thrown about

explanation.surface: Charlie fires off wild shots at a couple of anchors.
explanation.definitionFit: News anchors who present a programme together are co-hosts, a pair sharing the job.

clue.text: Hawk is close to finding headless fish

parts.note: in a hunting game, a searcher near the hidden thing is told they are warm

indicators.note: headless means the first letter of the fish is dropped

parts.note: a conger is a large sea eel, a kind of fish

explanation.surface: A bird of prey is about to catch a fish with no head.
explanation.definitionFit: In politics a hawk is someone who favours war, so it is another word for a militarist.

clue.text: Dipper left in Scottish stream

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for left inside the stream

parts.note: a lade is a Scottish word for a mill stream or channel

explanation.surface: A dipper, a bird of fast streams, has been left in a Scottish burn.
explanation.walkthrough: The dipper is a river bird that wades in streams, but here it is something that dips into soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladle is a deep-bowled spoon for dipping into a pot and serving liquid.

clue.text: Exercise book found in ancient battlefield rocks science

parts.note: PE stands for physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: found in puts the book inside the ancient city

parts.note: Troy was the site of the Trojan War
a log is a record book, like a ship's log

explanation.surface: A school exercise book discovered on an old battleground tells the science of stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrology is the branch of geology that studies the origin and composition of stones.

clue.text: Insect crosses screen over swallow

indicators.note: crosses means the insect's letters stretch across, going round the other piece

parts.note: a bee is a common insect

indicators.note: over signals that the word for screen is turned back to front

parts.note: a veil is a screen or covering

explanation.surface: An insect flies across a screen above a swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' looks like a bird beside the insect, but it is the verb meaning to accept a story; 'over' turns the screen word round.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow a story is to accept it as true, an informal synonym for credit or accept.

clue.text: Bear with blackbird

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the rook is a black bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A bear accompanied by a blackbird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blackbird' splits into black (B) and bird (ROOK). 'Bear' is a verb here, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To brook something is to tolerate or put up with it, usually in the negative: brook no argument.

clue.text: Local bosses catch doctor propped up in Rising Sun

parts.note: to land a fish is to catch it

indicators.note: in places the turned doctor inside the turned sun
rising in a down clue means reading upwards, so the word for sun goes backwards

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun

indicators.note: propped up in a down clue means stood upward, so the doctor's letters run backwards

explanation.surface: Pub managers grab a medic slumped at the bar of the Rising Sun inn.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'local' is one's neighbourhood pub, and its landlord runs it. 'Rising' turns SOL to LOS, and 'propped up' turns DR to RD.
explanation.definitionFit: Landlords are the licensees who run pubs, and a local is a regular pub.

clue.text: René Magritte's behind purge

indicators.note: the 's stands for has: the painter's name has the answer inside it

explanation.surface: René Magritte's clean-out of his backside.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of René and the start of Magritte.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema is a fluid injected into the rectum to empty the bowels, a purge of the rear end.

clue.text: Catches footloose spouse climbing pole

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means reading upwards, so the shortened spouse goes backwards
footloose means losing the foot, the last letter of the word for spouse

parts.note: a partner is a spouse
S is the south pole

explanation.surface: A carefree husband or wife shinning up a pole gets caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'footloose' drops the final R of PARTNER, and 'climbing' turns PARTNE upwards to ENTRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap someone is to catch them in a trap or trick.

clue.text: Old king finds duck among some swans

indicators.note: among puts the duck inside the group of swans

parts.note: a herd is one collective noun for a group of swans
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O

explanation.surface: An elderly monarch spots a duck in the middle of a group of swans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is the cricket score of zero, so O, rather than a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Herod the Great was a king of Judea in Biblical times, an ancient ruler.

clue.text: Shorten it — otherwise it's most unpleasant

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged in another way, so the letters of the first two words are reordered

explanation.surface: Advice to trim something, since the alternative is the worst option.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorny problem is a difficult, prickly one, so the superlative describes the most troublesome or disagreeable.

clue.text: Large bird covers one with masonry

indicators.note: covers means the bird's letters go around the other pieces

parts.note: the stork is a large wading bird
taken as written

explanation.surface: A big bird shelters something along with some stone building work.
explanation.definitionFit: Masonry is building work made of stone, the same thing as stonework.

clue.text: Catch criminal flicking a tree creeper

indicators.note: flicking suggests flipping the word over so that it reads backwards

parts.note: to nail a criminal is to catch him or her

explanation.surface: Arrest the wrongdoer who is flicking a small bird off a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: A treecreeper is a small bird, but here 'tree creeper' is the definition: a vine that climbs trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody climbing vine of tropical forests that creeps up tree trunks.

clue.text: Seal is backing a short breather

indicators.note: backing means the word is runs backwards
short means the last letter of the word for breather is cut off

parts.note: a gill is the breathing organ of a fish

explanation.surface: A seal is supporting a brief rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last L from GILL to give GIL. 'breather' looks like a pause but is the gill a fish breathes through.
explanation.definitionFit: A sigil is a seal or signet, a sign used to authenticate something.

clue.text: Battle to plug deficit at American research facility

indicators.note: to plug means the battle fills a gap inside the deficit

parts.note: a loss is a deficit
the Alamo was the 1836 battle in Texas

explanation.surface: A fight to fill a funding gap at an American laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: Los Alamos in New Mexico is the US national laboratory where the atomic bomb was developed.

clue.text: They turn hummingbirds jaws without resistance

parts.note: humming is British slang for smelly, and food that smells is off

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the birds' jaws go round the resistance

parts.note: birds use their beaks as jaws
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: The jaws of hummingbirds work without meeting resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hummingbirds' must be split into humming and birds. 'without' is used in its old sense of outside. Off breaks are cricket deliveries that turn.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an off break is a ball that spins from the off side after pitching, so such balls turn.

clue.text: Turkey might be let out of oven

parts.note: to free is to let out
a range is a large cooking stove with ovens

explanation.surface: A turkey might get released from the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: Free-range poultry are allowed to roam outdoors, as some turkeys are raised.

clue.text: Lark calling beneath arched fold of rock

parts.note: a lark is a prank, or antic
a line of work is a calling or vocation

explanation.surface: A lark singing beneath a curving rock formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beneath' in a down clue sets LINE below ANTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology an anticline is a fold of strata arched upward like an inverted U.

clue.text: Reptiles moving around end of Pompey's colonnade

indicators.note: around means the reshuffled letters go round the final letter of Pompey
moving means the letters of reptiles are shifted into a new order
end of picks the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Reptiles slither around the end of a Roman general's row of columns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges REPTILES to PERISTLE, and 'around' wraps that round Y, the last letter of Pompey.
explanation.definitionFit: A peristyle is a row of columns surrounding a courtyard or building, a type of colonnade.

clue.text: Chose to be decorated with feathers, parrot's head included

indicators.note: included means the parrot's first letter goes inside the feathered word

parts.note: plumed means adorned with plumes, or feathers

indicators.note: head picks the first letter of parrot

explanation.surface: A parrot opted to be feathered with its head showing.
explanation.definitionFit: To plump for something is to choose it decisively, so the past tense means picked.

clue.text: Locates it among uneven steps

indicators.note: among places the word it inside the other letters
uneven means the odd-numbered letters of steps: first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Someone finds it on a set of uneven stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uneven' takes letters 1, 3 and 5 of steps, S, E and S, and IT goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To site something is to place or position it, so sites works as a verb meaning places or positions.

clue.text: Backing musician attaches wing on rook, say

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the wing above the chess piece

parts.note: a side is a wing, as of a building or team
a rook is an example of a chessman, or man

explanation.surface: A session player fixes a wing to a rook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rook' is a chess piece, which is called a man, not a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideman is a supporting musician in a band, playing behind the leader.

clue.text: Uniform with medal and large cluster of flowers

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an MBE is a British honour awarded with a medal
L is the abbreviation for large, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A uniform worn with a medal and a big bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbel is a flat-topped flower head with stalks spreading from one point, as in cow parsley.

clue.text: Crow shot inside court

definitions.meaning: in squash a ... is a shot that hits a side wall before the front wall

explanation.walkthrough: Squash is a racket sport played inside a walled court; the boast is one of its strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: To boast is to brag or crow, and a boast is also an angled squash shot.

clue.text: Undressed by coffee counter, being shameless

parts.note: undressed means naked, or bare

indicators.note: counter means running the opposite way, so the word for coffee goes backwards

parts.note: decaf is decaffeinated coffee

explanation.surface: Someone disrobed beside the coffee bar, behaving without shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter' looks like a café's serving counter but is the reversal signal on the coffee word.
explanation.definitionFit: A barefaced lie is told without any attempt at disguise; the adjective describes brazen, unashamed behaviour.

clue.text: It follows a heron out of river to breed

parts.note: in the alphabet the letter after A is B

indicators.note: out of means the river abbreviation leaves the bird's name

parts.note: an egret is a kind of heron

explanation.surface: A creature trails a heron out of a river to mate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It follows a' means the letter after A in the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: To beget is to father or produce offspring, an old word for to breed.

clue.text: Bunting runs out of energy

definitions.meaning: bunting is decorative strings of small cloth pennants
to tire or droop, as a runner does late in a race

explanation.walkthrough: A bunting is also a small bird, but here it is decorative cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Flags are the cloth pennants in bunting; to flag is to tire and lose vigour.

clue.text: Grouse about main part with legend

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned around into a new order

parts.note: the end of leg is its final letter, G

explanation.surface: A game bird circles the main part carrying a legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legend' splits as leg end: the end of 'leg' is G. MAIN PART plus G is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The ptarmigan is a grouse of mountain and Arctic regions that turns white in winter.

clue.text: It's self-evident — Douglas here wants a kiss first

indicators.note: first places the earlier pieces ahead of the island

parts.note: X is the conventional kiss at the end of a letter
Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man, abbreviated IOM

explanation.surface: Something obvious: a man named Douglas wants a kiss before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man, a British Crown dependency in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a statement accepted as true without proof because it seems obviously correct.

clue.text: After a little rotation, sharpen the file

indicators.note: after puts the sharpen word behind the turned piece
rotation means the phrase for a little is turned to run backwards

parts.note: a tad means a little
to set a blade is to sharpen it

explanation.surface: Once it has been turned a little, put an edge on the metal file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotation' turns A TAD into DATA. The 'file' here is a computer file, not a metalworking tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A data set is a collection of related records held together, as in a computer file.

clue.text: Oriental seabird follows stormy sea

indicators.note: follows puts the bird after the mixed letters
stormy suggests the letters of sea are tossed into a new order

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A seabird flies behind a rough sea in the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and eastern both describe things from or relating to the East.
